summary: Corrado Pensa was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. Attested in 1971, he was Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome.

Craig J. Reynolds is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Amherst College (~1959–1963) and Cornell University (~1965–1973). He held a post at the Australian National University around 1989.

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested at the University of Cambridge from 2002, he served as curator of its South Asia manuscript collection in 2012, when he was also a fellow of Queens' College, Cambridge.
Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia, where he was taught by Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Cristina Pecchia is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. She earned her PhD at Sapienza University of Rome (~1999–2003) and studied at the University of Vienna (2000). Around 2009, she was a project researcher at IKGA.

Csaba Dezső is an Indologist who earned master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1992–1999) and a PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1998–2004). He became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2002.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (2003–2009). He served as a research assistant at Eötvös Loránd University and held a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024).

Cuilan Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She served as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 2017) and held a post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).
Culadasa (1944–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu. In 2011, he was attested as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha.
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).

Cuong T. Mai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaii and a PhD from Indiana University under John R. McRae (attested 2009), later serving as an adjunct lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied under John M. Rosenfield and Keizaburō Mizuno. She held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).

Cynthia Col is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who was a student in Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003), where she studied under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

Cyril Henry Philips (1912–2005) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool (~1930–1933) and SOAS (~1934–1938). He served as Director of SOAS (~1956–1976) and held a post at the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Washington (-1996) under Leonard van der Kuijp and Turrell V. Wylie. He has served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she also served as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau (1921–2010) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1939–1946). He held posts at SOAS University of London (~1950–1978) and University College London (1970–1978).
D. C. Sarasvati is an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan (attested 1978). In 1964–1965, she served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras.

D. Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He taught in the Department of Religion and served as Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College (~1970–2005).

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a doctoral student under Victor H. Mair.
